messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content: At a pressure of **10 kPa** the freezing (melting) point of pure water is only slightly below the standard 0 °C.  Using the water phase‑diagram (or a Clausius–Clapeyron estimate) gives a freezing point of roughly **–2 °C** (about –1.9 °C to –2.1 °C depending on the exact calculation).
